newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures post hefty losses.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures post hefty losses.

text.p: IMM currency futures started the week with hefty losses, with most contracts finishing near three week lows.

Mark weakness led the declines. News that Italy on Sunday had gained re-entry into the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) sparked mark sales against lira and helped the dollar make strides against the mark, traders said. Dollar/mark triggered several levels of buy-stops on the rally. One trader said dollar/mark looked on track for 1.5250.
One trader called currency futures volume "solid," a surprise considering the upcoming U.S. holiday, he said.

U.S. markets will be closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving Day holiday, and futures markets close early on Wednesday and Friday. Traders said thin trading pits could turn action choppy or lethargic as the week progresses.
Others cautioned that positioning could kick in before Wednesday's "tankan," Japan's business sentiment survey.
Some traders said any signs of economic strength in Japan reflected in the survey could be overshadowed by ongoing credit woes there.
Support in December yen was pegged at $0.008876, the 113.00 cash equivalent.

December marks slid as low as $0.6570 and closed just above there at $0.6574. Traders had said earlier in the day that $0.6600 was a key support level for the contract to hold. Support for early Tuesday was expected at $0.6550. A more intermediate floor was pegged at $0.6504, the October 17 session low.
Sterling continued its retreat from multi-year highs set last week.
Traders said profit-taking and belief that recent gains had been overdone were halting that rally.

At settlement, December yen settled off $0.000094 at $0.008899, marks finished off $0.0070 at $0.6574, Swiss francs were $0.0111 lower at $0.7778, sterling fell $0.0108 at $1.6680, Canadian dollars were down $0.0006 at $0.7461, Australian dollars were down $0.0034 at $0.8102 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000125 at $0.124950. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
